transcript.text: Our Dyson (one of the V ones, purple bits) keeps cutting out after about 5-10 seconds. Not every time - some days it does a whole room fine. It's maybe 5 years old. Already cleaned the filter and checked for blockages. Battery or something else?

To answer your question directly: yes, an intermittent fault like this on a five-year-old Dyson is very often the battery or how it connects to the machine. Because it sometimes works for a whole room but other times cuts out after just 10 seconds, it suggests either the battery cells are degrading (losing voltage under load) or there is an intermittent connection at the contacts. Reinsert it firmly until it clicks into place, then try running it again. If it still cuts out after 5-10 seconds even with clean contacts, the battery is likely failing and needs replacement.

Ok, I've reseated the battery and it clicks in fine. Battery isn't swollen or hot. Still cuts out though, and on Max it nearly always stops within a few seconds. Is that enough to say it's the battery?
Yes, that is enough to say it is the battery.
